correctness.rationale: On S² with area-normalized longitude lune 0<alpha<=pi, integration using uniform longitude and polar density sin(theta)/2 gives centroid m=(pi sin(alpha/2)/(2alpha),0,0) and second-moment matrix diag((1+sin(alpha)/alpha)/3,(1-sin(alpha)/alpha)/3,1/3). Independence gives E||X-Y||²=2-2||m||² and Var||X-Y||²=4(tr(M²)-||m||⁴), proving both stated formulas. For t=alpha/2, q=(sin t/t)², exact derivative factorization dV(2t)/dt=q qprime[8H(t)/9-pi^4/32] holds, H=(t cot t)²+t³/(tan t-t) strictly decreases from 4 to 0 by explicit derivative inequalities; unique crossing produces a strict nondegenerate global minimum. Endpoints give Var(pi)=13/12 and limit Var(0+)=20/9-pi^4/64; the latter is lower than hemisphere, so maximum is unique there. Independent scipy root gives alpha=1.1164752259454593, variance=0.6753158386946392, matching the result; finite checks only corroborate the all-angle proof.
